subject: humanities
passage: Every twenty years, the main sanctuaries of the Ise Grand Shrine in Japan are rebuilt from new timber on a site beside the old ones, after which the previous buildings are dismantled. The practice has continued, with some interruptions, for some 1,300 years. To conservation theorist Mark Ellery, who holds that a monument's authenticity resides in the original material surviving from its making, the shrine is a remarkable tradition but not an ancient building, since nothing that stands there today is more than two decades old.
passage_b: Ellery's standard works well for a cathedral whose stones were laid once, but it assumes that every culture locates a building's value in the same place. At Ise, what is preserved is the design, the carpentry techniques passed from master to apprentice, and the ritual of renewal itself; letting old timber stand would break the very tradition that makes the shrine what it is. Judged by what its builders aim to keep, the shrine is among the most faithfully preserved structures in the world.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the judgment of the shrine in Text 1?

choices.A: By disputing Text 1's account of how often the shrine is rebuilt and for how long
choices.B: By contending that his standard ignores what the shrine's tradition actually seeks to preserve
choices.C: By agreeing that only original material confers authenticity but claiming that Ise retains some
choices.D: By rejecting the idea that original material matters to the authenticity of any building

explanation.why: Text 2 says Ellery's standard "assumes that every culture locates a building's value in the same place." At Ise, what is kept is "the design, the carpentry techniques ... and the ritual of renewal," so judged by "what its builders aim to keep," the shrine is faithfully preserved. Text 2 argues that a material-based standard misses what this tradition preserves.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 accepts the facts of the rebuilding and argues only about how to judge them.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 argues that the shrine preserves design, skill, and ritual rather than timber, so a standard based on original material misjudges it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 does not claim any original material survives, and it denies that material is the only measure of authenticity.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says Ellery's standard "works well for a cathedral," so it does not reject the importance of material everywhere.
